items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: The Constitution provides collective responsibility to Lok Sabha without naming this motion. Lok Sabha Rule 198 expressly provides the motion against the Council of Ministers as a whole. At least 50 members must rise for leave. That is the admission threshold.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Can specify the conduct or policy of an individual minister, several ministers or the Council of Ministers. There is no dedicated censure rule. Lok Sabha handles it under the general rules for motions.
items.authority: LS Rules 184–189, Practice and Procedure of Parliament
items.raw_authority: LS Rules 184–189, Practice and Procedure of Parliament

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: A Lok Sabha device for a definite matter of urgent public importance, with the Speaker's consent. At least 50 members must rise for leave under Rule 60. Adjournment of a sitting is a different act.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: A member with the Chair's permission calls a minister's attention to an urgent matter. This is provided in both Houses.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: A formal discussion without a formal motion or vote.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Starred means oral answer and possible supplementaries. Unstarred means written answer without supplementaries. Short-notice questions concern urgent public importance.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: An established parliamentary practice. In Lok Sabha it generally follows Question Hour. The official FAQ describes the term as lacking formal recognition in parliamentary procedure.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Lok Sabha uses Rule 377 for matters that cannot be raised under specified other rules. Rajya Sabha has its own Special Mention procedure under Rules 180A–180E.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Suspension of a rule in its application to a motion related to listed business, subject to Chairman's consent. The proviso excludes cases with a specific suspension provision.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: The office and the duty to choose a member as soon as may be are constitutional. The Speaker fixes the Deputy Speaker's election date under Rule 8. Giving the post to the opposition has been a convention.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: The 1977 Act refers to the leader of the opposition party with the greatest numerical strength, recognised by the presiding officer. Section 2 prescribes no 10% threshold.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: The Tenth Schedule expressly uses political party and recognises voting directions issued by a party or authorised person or authority. The separate 1998 Facilities Act expressly names chief whips. For voting or abstaining contrary to a direction, prior permission or condonation within 15 days can avoid disqualification.
items.authority: Tenth Sch., para. 2(1)(b), Leaders and Chief Whips (Facilities) Act 1998
items.raw_authority: Tenth Sch., para. 2(1)(b), Leaders and Chief Whips (Facilities) Act 1998

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.prompt: Private member and private member's Bill
items.distinction: A member who is not a minister is a private member. An MP from the ruling party can qualify.
items.authority: Lok Sabha Rules and FAQ · PYQ 2017

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Freedom of speech in Parliament and immunity for speech or votes are express constitutional protections subject to the constitutional framework. Art. 105(3) allows other privileges to be defined by law. House rules prescribe privilege procedure.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: The disqualification is in the Constitution. The expression has no comprehensive constitutional definition. Parliament can exempt offices by law.
items.authority: Arts. 102(1)(a), 191(1)(a), Parliament (Prevention of Disqualification) Act, 1959 · PYQ 2019

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Attorney-General is a constitutional office and serves during the President's pleasure. Art. 76 does not require resignation when the appointing government resigns. The Solicitor-General is governed by the Law Officers Rules.
items.authority: Arts. 76, 88, Law Officers (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1987 · PYQ 2022
items.raw_authority: Arts. 76, 88, Law Officers (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1987 · **PYQ 2022**

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Art. 352(3) defines the Union Cabinet for written emergency advice. Cabinet committees are provided for in executive business rules under Art. 77(3).
items.authority: Art. 352(3), Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1961
items.raw_authority: Art. 352(3), Government of India (Transaction of Business) Rules, 1961

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: PAC and Committee on Public Undertakings each have up to 22 MPs, up to 15 from LS and up to 7 from RS. Estimates Committee has up to 30 MPs, all from LS. A minister cannot be a member of any of these three.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Up to 30 MPs. The full composition is 20 LS members and 10 RS members. Lok Sabha Speaker appoints its chair. Ministers are ineligible. Term is at most one year.
items.authority: LS Rules 331A–331B and general committee rules · PYQ 2026
items.raw_authority: LS Rules 331A–331B and general committee rules · **PYQ 2026**

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Constitution, parliamentary rules, law or convention?
items.distinction: Budget, Monsoon and Winter are usual names. Art. 85 prescribes a maximum six-month gap between the last sitting of one session and first sitting of the next, with no annual minimum sitting days.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: ECI supervises elections to Parliament, state legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President. State Election Commissions supervise panchayat and municipal elections.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: Union Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier. State Finance Commission is constituted by the Governor every fifth year and also reviews municipal finances.
items.authority: Arts. 280, 243I, 243Y · PYQ 2025 for the state appointing authority
items.raw_authority: Arts. 280, 243I, 243Y · **PYQ 2025** for the state appointing authority

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: Constitutional body chaired by the Union Finance Minister. If voting, the Union has one-third of vote weight and states together two-thirds. A decision requires at least three-fourths of weighted votes of members present and voting.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.prompt: SC, ST and backward classes commissions
items.distinction: NCSC, NCST and NCBC are constitutional under Arts. 338, 338A and 338B respectively. NCBC had a statutory predecessor.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: NHRC is statutory under the 1993 Act. NCDRC is statutory under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Law Commission is constituted by executive notification.
items.authority: PHRA 1993, s. 3, CPA 2019, s. 53, Law Commission website · PYQ 2023
items.raw_authority: PHRA 1993, s. 3, CPA 2019, s. 53, Law Commission website · **PYQ 2023**

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: Statutory bodies under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990, National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992, and Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 respectively.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: Statutory under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, CVC Act, 2003, RTI Act, 2005, and NGT Act, 2010 respectively.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: Constituted by Union Cabinet resolution dated 1 January 2015.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.prompt: Inter-State Council, Zonal Councils, North Eastern Council
items.distinction: Inter-State Council was established by presidential order under Art. 263 in 1990. Zonal Councils are under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. NEC has its own 1971 Act.
items.authority: Art. 263, States Reorganisation Act, s. 15, NEC Act 1971
items.raw_authority: Art. 263, States Reorganisation Act, s. 15, NEC Act 1971

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: Arts. 82 and 170 provide the framework for readjustment under a parliamentary law. The Commission for the last completed nationwide exercise was set up under the Delimitation Act, 2002.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: CAG is a constitutional auditor. Detailed duties are statutory. PAC is a parliamentary committee that examines specified accounts and CAG reports. President or Governor causes relevant CAG reports to be laid before the appropriate legislature.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: A joint PSC can be created by parliamentary law after resolutions of the legislatures of the participating states. President appoints members of UPSC and joint PSC. Governor appoints State PSC members. President removes PSC members under Art. 317.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by President under Art. 350B. President initially specifies SC/ST lists for a state or UT. Parliament subsequently includes or excludes entries by law.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Bodies with similar names and different legal origins
items.distinction: President specifies the Central List under Art. 342A, and Parliament can amend it. A state or UT can prepare and maintain its own list for its own purposes by law.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: President, Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. President is a component of Parliament and holds no seat in either House.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: The Chair adjourns a sitting, including sine die. President prorogues a House. Only Lok Sabha is subject to dissolution. Prorogation can occur without prior adjournment sine die.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: Prorogation itself does not lapse Bills. On LS dissolution, a Bill pending in LS or passed by LS and pending in RS lapses, subject to Art. 108(5). A Bill pending in RS and never passed by LS survives. A notified joint sitting can proceed despite later dissolution.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: While presiding, casting vote on a tie. During consideration of removal of the Speaker, the Speaker cannot preside, can speak, and can vote in the first instance only.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: Speaker continues until just before the first meeting of the new Lok Sabha. Removal needs 14 days' notice and a majority of all the then members of the House.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: Art. 110 uses only listed matters and incidental matters. Introduced only in LS with President's recommendation. RS has 14 days to recommend changes. Speaker certifies. President cannot return it for reconsideration.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: Includes a matter in Art. 110(1)(a)–(f) and other provisions. Introduced only in LS with President's recommendation, subject to the tax-reduction amendment proviso. RS has ordinary legislative powers, and joint sitting can apply.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: Involves expenditure from Consolidated Fund of India. Can be introduced in either House. President's recommendation is required before that House passes the Bill.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: For qualifying deadlocks on ordinary Bills and eligible Financial Bills. Money Bills and Art. 368 Bills are excluded. Lok Sabha Speaker normally presides.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: Constitution uses Annual Financial Statement. LS votes demands for grants. Charged expenditure can be discussed without a vote. Appropriation by law permits withdrawal from the Consolidated Fund.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.prompt: Consolidated Fund, Public Account, Contingency Fund
items.distinction: Revenue, loans raised and loan repayments received go into Consolidated Fund. Other public moneys received by or on behalf of the government go into Public Account. Contingency Fund is an imprest for advances pending legislative authorisation.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: For ordinary Assembly Bills, first delay up to three months, second up to one month. The Constitution provides no joint sitting of state Houses. For Money Bills, Council recommends within 14 days.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.prompt: Create or abolish a State Legislative Council
items.distinction: Assembly first resolves by majority of total membership plus at least two-thirds present and voting. Parliament then legislates by ordinary law.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.prompt: MPs may speak or vote where?
items.distinction: Ministers and Attorney-General can speak and participate in either House, joint sittings and committees of which they are named members. Art. 88 itself confers no vote. Ministers vote on the basis of membership.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Parliament and state legislatures
items.distinction: Art. 249 resolution opens Parliament's State List power in the national interest. Art. 312 resolution permits Parliament to create an All India Service by law. Both need at least two-thirds of RS members present and voting.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: President uses elected MPs and elected MLAs of states plus Delhi and Puducherry. Vice-President uses members of both Houses of Parliament, including nominated MPs, and excludes MLAs. Both use proportional representation by single transferable vote and secret ballot.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: Impeachment can start in either House for violation of the Constitution. Each House needs at least two-thirds of total membership at its relevant stage. VP removal starts in RS by majority of all then members and must be agreed to by LS. Both procedures require at least 14 days' notice.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: President can require reconsideration of ministerial advice once and must act on the advice tendered after reconsideration.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: President can return a non-Money ordinary Bill once and cannot withhold assent after Parliament repasses it. President must assent to a duly passed Art. 368 Bill. Governor's options under Art. 200 and President's under Art. 201 involve a separate framework.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: Under the Supreme Court's November 2025 Art. 143 opinion, there are no judicially prescribed general deadlines or deemed assent. Prolonged, unexplained and indefinite inaction by a Governor can invite a limited judicial direction to act.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: President can promulgate unless both Houses are in session. Governor uses the parallel rule for the state legislature. Six weeks run from reassembly, using the later date if Houses reassemble separately. The ordinance has the force of an Act within legislative competence. It remains subject to fundamental rights and cannot amend the Constitution under Art. 368.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: President covers court-martial sentences, offences within Union executive competence and all death sentences. Governor's Art. 161 power concerns offences within state executive competence. Art. 72(3) preserves state-law power to suspend, remit or commute a death sentence.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: Union Council of Ministers cap is 15% of LS strength. State cap is 15% of Assembly strength, with a minimum of 12. A minister who is not a member of the relevant legislature for six consecutive months ceases to be a minister. The Constitution does not classify ministers into four ranks.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: For Art. 102(1) disqualifications of sitting MPs, President decides according to ECI opinion. For Art. 191(1) of sitting MLAs/MLCs, Governor decides according to ECI opinion. Defection is decided by the relevant Chair or Speaker under the Tenth Schedule, subject to judicial review. If the question concerns the presiding officer, the House elects another member to decide.
items.authority: Arts. 103, 192, Tenth Sch. para. 6, Kihoto Hollohan
items.raw_authority: Arts. 103, 192, Tenth Sch. para. 6, Kihoto Hollohan

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: Voluntarily giving up membership can be inferred from conduct. An independent member is disqualified on joining a party after election. A nominated member can join within six months of taking the seat. Merger exception requires at least two-thirds of the legislature party. The old one-third split exception was removed.
items.authority: Tenth Sch. paras. 2, 4, 91st Amendment · PYQ 2022 for nominated members
items.raw_authority: Tenth Sch. paras. 2, 4, 91st Amendment · **PYQ 2022** for nominated members

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: The Tenth Schedule fixes no deadline. The Supreme Court has said the Speaker should ordinarily decide within three months, absent exceptional circumstances.
items.authority: Tenth Sch. para. 6, Keisham Meghachandra Singh · PYQ 2022 for the Schedule
items.raw_authority: Tenth Sch. para. 6, Keisham Meghachandra Singh · **PYQ 2022** for the Schedule

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: 1950 Act principally covers allocation of seats and electoral rolls. 1951 Act covers conduct of elections, qualifications and disqualifications, election disputes and party registration.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: Registration with ECI comes from s. 29A. National/state party recognition and reserved symbols come from the Election Symbols Order.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: ECI is constitutional. Under the 2023 Act, President appoints on recommendation of a committee of PM, Lok Sabha Opposition Leader and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM. The statute is under challenge. The 2023 Anoop Baranwal formula with CJI applied until Parliament made a law.
items.authority: Art. 324, 2023 Act ss. 4, 7, Anoop Baranwal, September 2026 proceedings
items.raw_authority: Art. 324, 2023 Act ss. 4, 7, Anoop Baranwal, September 2026 proceedings

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.prompt: Removal of CEC and other ECs
items.distinction: CEC removal follows the manner and grounds applicable to a Supreme Court judge. Other ECs and regional commissioners can be removed only on CEC recommendation.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: 18 for electoral-roll registration subject to law. 25 for LS/Assembly. 30 for RS/Legislative Council. 35 for President, VP and Governor.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Executive, elections and disqualification
items.distinction: LS and Assembly use first-past-the-post, so 50% of votes polled is unnecessary. The ordinary cap is two constituencies in the same election of the type covered by s. 33(7).
items.authority: RPA 1951 s. 33(7), Conduct of Elections Rules 1961 r. 64 · PYQ 2017, 2021
items.raw_authority: RPA 1951 s. 33(7), Conduct of Elections Rules 1961 r. 64 · **PYQ 2017, 2021**

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Parliament, including residuary taxing power. GST is separately dealt with by Art. 246A. Parliament alone legislates for GST on inter-State supplies.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Five distinct routes to remember are Rajya Sabha national-interest resolution, national emergency, request by two or more state legislatures, implementing international obligations, and exercise of state legislative power under President's Rule.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Art. 249 resolution lasts up to a year at a time, with renewals possible. The law ceases to have effect to the extent of incompetency six months after the resolution ends. Art. 252 legislation starts from resolutions of at least two states. Other states may adopt it. Only Parliament can amend or repeal it under that article.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: A conflicting state law reserved for and receiving presidential assent prevails in that state, subject to Parliament's power to override it.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: War, external aggression or armed rebellion. Written decision of Union Cabinet is required. Parliamentary approval normally within one month, then renewal every six months. Each House uses a majority of total membership plus at least two-thirds present and voting. Special rules apply if LS is dissolved.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Failure of constitutional machinery in a state. Can be proclaimed on the Governor's report or otherwise. Normally approved within two months and renewed every six months. Three-year outer limit, with additional conditions for continuation beyond one year.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Threat to financial stability or credit of India or any part. Normally approved within two months. The Constitution prescribes no periodic renewal.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Art. 19 restrictions are relaxed by Art. 358 only for emergency on grounds of war or external aggression, subject to the constitutional limits. Art. 359 involves a presidential order suspending access to courts to enforce specified Part III rights. Arts. 20 and 21 are excluded.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.prompt: Altering state boundaries vs giving up territory
items.distinction: Art. 3 legislation requires President's recommendation and referral to the affected state legislature for views in applicable cases. The state's consent is unnecessary. Cession of Indian territory to a foreign country requires a constitutional amendment.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Bill can start in either House. Each House must separately pass it by majority of total membership and at least two-thirds present and voting. No joint sitting. Initiation is in Parliament without prior presidential recommendation. The President must assent once the requirements are met.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: At least half of state legislatures for listed federal changes. Includes Arts. 54, 55, 73, 162, 241 and 279A, specified judiciary chapters, Centre–state legislative relations, Seventh Schedule lists, representation of states in Parliament, and Art. 368 itself.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Parliamentary quorum is generally one-tenth, subject to law. Removal of the Speaker uses a majority of all then members. Art. 368 combines a majority of total membership with two-thirds present and voting. GST Council has a separate weighted vote.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.distinction: Basic-structure limitation comes from Supreme Court doctrine. Ninth Schedule laws inserted after 24 April 1973 can be tested under the I.R. Coelho framework.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Federal powers, emergencies and amendment
items.prompt: Delimitation freeze vs seat reservation for women
items.distinction: Arts. 82 and 170 refer to publication of relevant figures of the first census taken after 2026 for the relevant freeze. Under Art. 334A, women's reservation takes effect after a delimitation exercise for that purpose following publication of figures of the first census taken after commencement of the 106th Amendment Act. The Act commenced on 16 April 2026 under S.O. 1922(E). Actual seat reservation still depends on Art. 334A's triggers. The 131st Amendment Bill failed in Lok Sabha in April 2026.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Art. 393 supplies the short title. Art. 394 gives 26 January 1950 as the general commencement date and names provisions that took effect immediately on adoption. Art. 395 repeals the Indian Independence Act 1947 and Government of India Act 1935 with the stated exception for the Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act 1949.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Includes ordinances, orders, bye-laws, rules, regulations, notifications and customs or usages having the force of law in India. Art. 13(4) excludes amendments under Art. 368 from Art. 13. Basic-structure review independently applies.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Part of the Constitution and amendable within basic-structure limits. The 42nd Amendment added Socialist, Secular and integrity. The Preamble guides interpretation and confers no independent power or enforceable right.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.prompt: Fundamental rights for citizens vs persons
items.distinction: Art. 19 is for citizens. Arts. 14, 20 and 21 protect persons. Separate rights have their own wording and exceptions. Art. 16 concerns public employment for citizens.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Classic examples are untouchability under Art. 17, Art. 23 prohibitions and Art. 24's bar on employment of a child below 14 in any factory, mine or other hazardous employment. Art. 15(2) also reaches specified forms of exclusion in public access.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Art. 21A covers free and compulsory education for ages 6–14. Art. 45 concerns early childhood care and education until six. Art. 51A(k) concerns the parent or guardian's duty to provide educational opportunities for ages 6–14.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: In Art. 51A, Part IVA. The 42nd Amendment added ten. The 86th added the education duty. The constitutional duties address citizens. Laws can give effect to them.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: DPSPs are non-justiciable and fundamental in governance. Art. 31C's limited protection concerns laws giving effect to Art. 39(b) or (c) against Arts. 14 and 19, subject to judicial scrutiny of the connection.
items.authority: Arts. 37, 39, 31C, Minerva Mills, Property Owners Association
items.raw_authority: Arts. 37, 39, 31C, Minerva Mills, Property Owners Association

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Constitutional right under Art. 300A, outside Part III. Deprivation requires authority of law.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Supreme Court under Art. 32 for Part III rights. High Courts under Art. 226 for Part III rights and other legal rights. HC territorial jurisdiction may rest on where the cause of action arises wholly or in part.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Habeas corpus tests detention and can reach private detention. Mandamus enforces public duty and can reach a private body performing that duty. Quo warranto tests entitlement to public office and does not require personal injury. Prohibition stops proceedings beyond jurisdiction. Certiorari quashes an offending decision or order.
items.authority: Arts. 32, 226, Supreme Court case law · PYQ 2022 for mandamus and quo warranto
items.raw_authority: Arts. 32, 226, Supreme Court case law · **PYQ 2022** for mandamus and quo warranto

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Retirement ages 65 and 62 respectively. President appoints both. Removal for proved misbehaviour or incapacity requires an address from each House in the same session by majority of total membership and at least two-thirds present and voting.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship
items.distinction: Art. 143 is a presidential reference. Art. 137 is Supreme Court review of its own judgments or orders. Art. 142 concerns complete justice in a pending cause or matter.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: Rights, duties, courts and citizenship

items.prompt: President — eligibility and office of profit

items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Supreme Court decides election disputes. A vacancy in the electoral college is insufficient by itself to challenge an election. Casual presidential vacancy is to be filled within six months and the successor gets a **full** term.

items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: President remains until successor enters office. VP acts as President on a vacancy. During discharge of presidential functions, VP does not perform RS Chair duties.

items.distinction: Impeachment for **violation of the Constitution**, initiated by either House. Notice signed by at least one-quarter of total membership of the initiating House, 14 days' notice, and at least two-thirds of **total membership** in each House at the relevant stage.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.prompt: President — elected by some, impeached by others

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: President may ask ministers to reconsider advice once and is bound by the advice after reconsideration. Art. 74(2) bars inquiry into whether and what advice was tendered.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Art. 111 permits return of a **non-Money Bill**. After passage again, the President shall not withhold assent. Art. 368 separately commands assent to a duly passed amendment.

items.prompt: President — ordinance while one House sits

items.subject: Polity

items.distinction: Covers court-martial sentences, offences within Union executive competence and all death sentences. Art. 72(3) preserves state-law powers to suspend, remit or commute a death sentence. Distinguish sentence reduction from full pardon.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Official-act personal non-answerability. Criminal proceedings barred during term. No arrest or imprisonment process during term. items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Members of both Houses, **including nominated members**, vote. State legislators do not vote. Qualification is for election to **Rajya Sabha**.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Resigns to President. Removal starts in RS by majority of **all then members**, then requires LS agreement. 14 days' notice. No constitutional list of grounds equivalent to presidential impeachment.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Ex officio RS Chair and usually a casting voter on a tie. While a resolution for own removal is under consideration, may speak and take part but cannot vote at all.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Appointed by President. Five years **subject to President's pleasure**, with holdover until successor enters. Resignation to President. Same person may be Governor of multiple states.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Citizen and at least 35. No constitutional requirement to be an outsider or to consult the Chief Minister before appointment. Cannot sit as an MP or MLA/MLC while Governor.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Tenure is subject to pleasure, without a parliamentary impeachment process. B.P. Singhal holds that withdrawal of pleasure cannot be arbitrary, capricious or unreasonable.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Ministerial aid and advice is the rule, with constitutionally recognised exceptions. Art. 163(2) cannot be read as a free-standing discretion to decide every matter personally.

items.subject: Polity

items.distinction: Art. 200 uses distinct routes for assent, reservation and withholding with return in the applicable non-Money Bill scenario. items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: No general court-imposed timelines or deemed assent under the November 2025 opinion. Prolonged, unexplained and indefinite inaction can invite a limited direction to act. The Governor retains personal immunity.

items.subject: Polity

items.prompt: Governor — ordinance timing and President's instructions
items.distinction: In a bicameral state the Governor can promulgate unless both Houses sit. Presidential instructions are required in the three specified categories under the first proviso to Art. 213(1).

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Powers under the Fifth Schedule, the Sixth Schedule and particular Art. 371 provisions have different triggers and procedures. A special responsibility in one state cannot be generalised to every Governor.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.prompt: PM and CM — who appoints whom
items.distinction: President appoints PM and other Union ministers on the PM's advice. Governor appoints CM and other state ministers on CM's advice. The Union Council is collectively responsible to **Lok Sabha**, state Council to **Legislative Assembly**.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: PM may sit in either House of Parliament. CM can sit in either state House in a bicameral state. The Constitution allows a non-member a maximum of six consecutive months as minister before ceasing to hold office.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: Union cap is 15% of **Lok Sabha**, state cap 15% of **Assembly** with a minimum of 12. Tribal welfare minister provision specifically names Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.prompt: PM and CM — duty to inform
items.distinction: PM communicates decisions and furnishes information to President. CM has corresponding duties towards Governor. Each submits a minister's decision to the Council if required by the relevant constitutional head.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B1. President, VP, Governor & Councils of Ministers
items.distinction: A member disqualified under the Tenth Schedule is also disqualified from appointment as minister for the period specified in Arts. 75(1B) or 164(1B). Earlier re-election can end the bar.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.prompt: Lok Sabha Speaker — resignation and removal
items.distinction: Speaker resigns to Deputy Speaker, and vice versa. Removal is by majority of **all then members** after 14 days' notice. Giving up House membership ordinarily vacates the office.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Speaker continues until just before the first meeting of the newly constituted Lok Sabha. The special protection expressly names the Speaker.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.prompt: SPEAKER vs RS CHAIR — own removal vote
items.distinction: Lok Sabha Speaker can speak and vote **in the first instance** while own removal is considered. The RS Chair can speak during the VP removal proceedings and **cannot vote** on any matter in those proceedings. Neither presides over own removal proceedings.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Deputy Speaker presides in the Speaker's absence. When presiding, Rule 10 gives the Deputy Speaker the same powers as Speaker for that sitting. There is no general constitutional rule of personal subordination while presiding.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Deputy Chair is chosen **by RS from its members** and resigns to Chair. RS can remove by majority of all then members after 14 days' notice. LS agreement is needed for VP removal, a separate process.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Assembly chooses its Speaker and Deputy Speaker. Legislative Council chooses its Chairman and Deputy Chairman. The Governor is never the ex officio Chair of a State Legislative Council.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Art. 110(3) makes the Speaker's decision final in the constitutional text. Judicial decisions distinguish finality inside the process from claims of constitutional illegality capable of review. Avoid assuming every disputed certificate is invalid or every certificate is immune.
items.authority: Arts. 110, 122, Raja Ram Pal, Rojer Mathew [J3]
items.raw_authority: Arts. 110, 122, Raja Ram Pal, Rojer Mathew [J3]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.prompt: SC/ST Welfare Committee — powers and composition
items.distinction: Full strength 30, with 20 from LS and 10 from RS. Speaker appoints the chair, ministers are ineligible and term is at most one year. Distinguish the parliamentary committee from NCSC and NCST.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: A member must take oath before taking the seat. A House **may** declare a seat vacant for absence from all meetings for 60 days without permission, excluding specified periods of prorogation or adjournment.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: President nominates 12 to Rajya Sabha for special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art or social service. The Anglo-Indian special representation provision ceased after the period set by Art. 334(b).

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Arts. 105(2) and 194(2) protect speech and voting in the House **or its committees**. Bribery in connection with legislative votes or speech is prosecutable under Sita Soren.
items.authority: Arts. 105, 194 · PYQ 2025 for legislative speech [J3, P5]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Art. 102(1) or 191(1) cases for sitting members go to President or Governor, who act according to **ECI's** opinion. Do not swap in the SEC for an MLA. Defection follows separate Tenth Schedule procedure.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: An elected independent member who joins a political party after election incurs disqualification. A nominated member may join within six months **from taking the seat**. For party voting directions, prior permission or condonation within 15 days can matter.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: At least two-thirds of the **legislature party** must agree to the merger for the deeming rule. The former one-third split exception was deleted.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B2. Presiding Officers, MPs & MLAs
items.distinction: Relevant Speaker or Chair decides, subject to review. If the question concerns that officer, the House elects a member to decide. The Schedule sets no fixed period. Supreme Court says ordinarily three months absent exceptional circumstances.
items.authority: Tenth Schedule para. 6, Kihoto Hollohan, Keisham · PYQ 2022 for text [J5, P2]
items.raw_authority: Tenth Schedule para. 6, Kihoto Hollohan, Keisham · **PYQ 2022** for text [J5, P2]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: President appoints a person qualified to be a **Supreme Court judge**. Art. 76 does not require a sitting or retired judge or a law minister. Distinguished jurist is one route in Art. 124(3).

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: Right of audience in **all courts in India** in performance of duties. May speak and take part in either House, joint sitting and a committee of which named a member. Art. 88 supplies no vote.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: Governor appoints someone qualified to be a **High Court judge**. Holds during Governor's pleasure. Art. 177 parallels legislative participation with no vote created by that Article.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: Law Officers Rules govern these posts. The constitutional participation clause names Attorney-General at Union level and Advocate-General at state level.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: President appoints by warrant. **Six years or 65, whichever is earlier**, is statutory under the 1971 Act. Same manner and grounds of removal as an SC judge are constitutional.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: Ineligible for further office under Union or state government. Constitutional protection against disadvantageous changes covers salary and specified rights. Administrative expenses are charged on Consolidated Fund of India.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: Accounts of Union and states are kept in the form the **President prescribes on the advice of CAG**. Art. 150 gives the prescription and advisory roles to different actors.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: Union reports go to President who causes laying before each House. State reports go to Governor who causes laying before the state legislature. PAC scrutinises reports. CAG has audit authority and no power to prosecute in its own right.
items.authority: Art. 151, CAG Act, LS Rules 308–309 · PYQ 2012 [S1, P4]
items.raw_authority: Art. 151, CAG Act, LS Rules 308–309 · **PYQ 2012** [S1, P4]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: India’s CAG does not pre-authorise every payment from the Consolidated Fund. Constitution controls appropriation. The CAG audits expenditure and other matters under law.
items.authority: Arts. 114, 149, 266 · PYQ 2012 for supposed exchequer control [P4]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B3. Attorney-General, Advocate-General, CAG & Audit
items.distinction: CAG’s government-company role under the Companies Act includes appointment of the auditor and directions, and supplementary audit or comments where applicable. Avoid equating it with the CAG personally doing all company audits.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.distinction: Citizen plus one of the stated routes. At least five years as High Court judge, at least ten years as High Court advocate, or distinguished jurist in President's opinion.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.distinction: Citizen plus at least ten years holding judicial office in India or at least ten years as a High Court advocate under the specified rules. No equivalent distinguished-jurist route in Art. 217.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.prompt: SC vs HC — age and transfer
items.distinction: Retirement 65 vs 62. President may transfer a High Court judge after consultation with CJI under Art. 222. The judicial decisions and appointment procedure elaborate consultation.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.distinction: President's order after an address from **each** House in the same session, by majority of total membership plus at least two-thirds present and voting, for proved misbehaviour or incapacity.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.distinction: Former Supreme Court judge cannot plead or act in any court or before any authority in India. Permanent former High Court judge may plead or act in the Supreme Court and High Courts other than the one where the restriction applies.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.prompt: Acting, ad hoc and retired judges
items.distinction: Acting CJI under Art. 126, an ad hoc SC judge under Art. 127 and attendance by retired judges under Art. 128 each have different authorisation and eligibility.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.prompt: SC and HC — courts of record
items.distinction: Both are courts of record with constitutional contempt powers. Their Articles differ. Art. 142 is the SC complete-justice provision.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.prompt: SC and HC — territorial reach of writs
items.distinction: Art. 32 is for enforcing Part III. Art. 226 reaches Part III and other legal rights, including where cause of action arises wholly or partly within territory under clause (2).

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.distinction: Presidential reference under Art. 143, appeal routes under Arts. 132–136, and review of SC's own judgment or order under Art. 137 have distinct triggers. Special leave under Art. 136 has an armed-forces court or tribunal exclusion.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.distinction: Governor appoints, posts and promotes in consultation with High Court. Direct recruitment from outside service requires at least seven years as advocate or pleader and High Court recommendation. Control over district and subordinate courts vests in High Court.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B4. Supreme Court, High Courts & Subordinate Judiciary
items.distinction: Art. 323A enables **Parliament** to legislate on administrative tribunals. Art. 323B refers to the **appropriate legislature** for specific matters. Constitutional judicial review remains under L. Chandra Kumar.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.prompt: Election Commission — who fixes size and appoints
items.distinction: Constitution specifies CEC and such number of other commissioners, if any, as President may fix. President appoints subject to parliamentary law. When other ECs are appointed, CEC is Chair.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.prompt: Election Commission — selection under the 2023 Act
items.distinction: PM chairs. Other members are a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by PM and Lok Sabha's Leader of Opposition, with a fallback for the largest opposition party where a recognised Leader is absent. Appointment is by President.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: Anoop Baranwal's CJI-inclusive formula operated until Parliament made a law. The 2023 Act uses its own selection committee. The Act has been challenged. The September 2026 proceedings concerned the route to a larger bench, rather than a ruling striking down s. 7.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.prompt: Election Commission — eligibility, term and salary
items.distinction: The 2023 Act sets an official rank and election-related knowledge and experience requirements. Term is six years or 65, whichever earlier. No reappointment. Combined EC and CEC service may not exceed six years. Salary is equivalent to an SC judge under s. 10.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: CEC has the same manner and grounds of removal as an SC judge. Other ECs and regional commissioners cannot be removed except on CEC recommendation. CEC's disadvantageous condition-of-service protection is expressly stated in Art. 324(5).

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: Parliament, state legislatures, President and VP. Municipal and panchayat elections sit with SEC. Presidential and VP election **disputes** go to SC.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: Governor appoints. Removal follows the manner and grounds of removal of a **High Court judge**. Service conditions may not be varied to disadvantage after appointment.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: ECI supervises elections. Constituting a delimitation commission and assigning delimitation powers depend on parliamentary law. Under the 2002 Act the ECI is represented on the Commission.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: ECI registers parties under s. 29A and administers recognition and reserved symbols under the Symbols Order. Eligibility, election petition and conviction consequences have separate statutory provisions.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: Parliamentary and state legislative elections are challenged by election petition to the High Court under the RPA. Appeal can lie to SC. President and VP election disputes start in SC.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.prompt: UPSC, SPSC and Joint PSC — formation
items.distinction: Each state has a PSC or arrangement within Art. 315. Parliament can provide a Joint PSC after resolutions from the participating state legislatures. President appoints Union and Joint PSC members. Governor appoints SPSC members.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.prompt: UPSC vs State or Joint PSC — term
items.distinction: Six years with age ceilings **65 for UPSC** and **62 for State or Joint PSC**. As nearly as possible half the members must have held government office for at least ten years.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: President removes members of **all** PSCs under Art. 317. Misbehaviour route requires SC inquiry on presidential reference. Governor can suspend a State PSC member in the relevant reference scenario, pending presidential decision.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: UPSC chair cannot take further government employment. State PSC chair can become UPSC chair or member or chair of another State PSC. Other members have specific upward appointment routes and general restrictions.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B5. Election & Public Service Commissions
items.distinction: Exam and consultation functions are distinct. Laws can add functions. Regulations can except matters from consultation. Reports go to President or Governor, with reasons for non-acceptance laid before the legislature.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: President constitutes it every fifth year **or earlier**. It consists of chairman plus four other members. Parliament determines qualifications and manner of selection by law.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Five-year interval relates to **constituting the Commission**, while individual appointments run for the period specified by President in the appointment order.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.prompt: Union Finance Commission — subject of advice
items.distinction: Tax sharing vertically and among states, principles of grants-in-aid, measures to augment state Consolidated Funds for panchayats and municipalities **on the basis of State Finance Commission recommendations**, and other matters referred by President in the interests of sound finance.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Population, area, income distance, forest and ecology, demographic performance, and tax and fiscal efforts. The 2023 question asked whether governance reforms and stable government were also criteria. The factors in an award are report-specific.
items.authority: Table 6.4, 15th Finance Commission report · PYQ 2023 [P3, S4]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.prompt: Union Finance Commission — report and action
items.distinction: President causes recommendations and an explanatory memorandum on action taken to be laid before each House. Tax devolution and release of grants require action under their applicable framework.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.prompt: State Finance Commission — who and when
items.distinction: Governor constitutes it within the relevant constitutional timeline and thereafter every fifth year. The same commission reviews municipal finances by Art. 243Y. Governor causes recommendations and action memorandum to be laid before state legislature.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Union Finance Minister is Chair. Union Minister of State in charge of Revenue or Finance and a minister nominated by each state are members. State members choose one among themselves as Vice-Chair.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Half of total membership is quorum. A decision needs at least three-fourths of **weighted votes of members present and voting**. Union has one-third of weight and states together two-thirds.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Recommendations guide cooperative federal action. Supreme Court in Mohit Minerals held that Art. 279A recommendations are not binding as such on Union and state legislatures. Distinguish a specific statute conditioning a delegated power on a recommendation.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Council shall establish a mechanism to adjudicate disputes arising from recommendations or their implementation. This is distinct from the interstate river-water tribunal system.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Art. 263 permits President to establish a council on public-interest grounds. The 1990 order assigned coordination and discussion functions under clauses (b) and (c). The Article's general list is wider than that order's assignment.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Five statutory Zonal Councils in the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 framework. Union Home Minister chairs in practice as the Union minister nominated under the Act.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Section 3 provides Governors and Chief Ministers of member states and three presidential nominees. President may also nominate a Union minister as member, shall nominate the Chair, and may nominate another member as Vice-Chair.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Parliament may legislate for adjudication and may exclude courts' jurisdiction over specified inter-state river-water disputes. The current statutory tribunal framework is under the 1956 Act.
items.authority: Art. 262, Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956
items.raw_authority: Art. 262, Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B6. Finance Commission, GST Council & Federal Institutions
items.distinction: Union Cabinet resolution constituted it. Prime Minister chairs. Its Governing Council follows the executive framework, distinct from the Finance Commission and GST Council.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Chair, Vice-Chair and **three other members**. President appoints by warrant under hand and seal. Civil-court powers apply when investigating or inquiring into specified matters.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: The analogous constitutional body for ST safeguards. Distinguish the Commission from local Tribes Advisory Councils and autonomous district councils.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Constitutional body after the 102nd Amendment. The earlier statutory NCBC is relevant to historical questions. Same broad position of Chair, Vice-Chair and three other members.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.prompt: NCSC, NCST, NCBC — reports and policy consultation
items.distinction: Reports go to President, with parliamentary laying and action/explanation framework. State-related reports also reach Governor for laying before state legislature. Government consultation on major policy matters has the Art. 338B(9) proviso for state/UT lists under Art. 342A(3).

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Powers of a civil court for specific inquiries do not create a civil court with ordinary decree-making or enforcement powers. Distinguish investigation, recommendation, and adjudication.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.prompt: SC and ST lists — who changes them
items.distinction: President initially specifies by public notification, after consultation with Governor where the Article requires it. **Parliament by law** subsequently includes or excludes entries.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Art. 342A(1)–(2) concerns the Central List. Art. 342A(3) permits every state or UT to prepare and maintain by law its own list for its own purposes.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: President may appoint a commission to investigate conditions of socially and educationally backward classes. That inquiry commission has a different basis from standing NCBC under Art. 338B.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: President appoints the Special Officer. Reports go to President, who causes laying before both Houses and sends them to governments of concerned states. This is separate from the statutory National Commission for Minorities.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Art. 344 has its own Commission and 30-member parliamentary committee. Under s. 4 of the Official Languages Act, a separately sourced Committee on Official Language has a similar 20 LS/10 RS composition. Check which instrument a question names.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Art. 30 uses religion or language. Art. 29(1) protects any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture. The statutory NCMEI and NCM serve different functions.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: TAC has up to 20 members, with about three-fourths ST representatives in the Assembly as the Schedule provides. The President declares a Scheduled Area. Governor regulations under para. 5 require presidential assent and consultation with TAC where one exists.
items.authority: Fifth Schedule paras. 4–6 · PYQ 2023 on who declares [P3]
items.raw_authority: Fifth Schedule paras. 4–6 · **PYQ 2023** on who declares [P3]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Applies to specified tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Council composition, law-making and Governor assent requirements depend on the Schedule and relevant area-specific provisions.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Parliament may by law form an autonomous state covering all or part of specified Sixth Schedule tribal areas within Assam and create a legislature, Council of Ministers or both. An autonomous district council is a different institution.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B7. SC, ST, SEBC, Languages & Minority Institutions
items.distinction: Delhi assembly has a special constitutional framework in Art. 239AA and no legislative competence over public order, police and land as specified. Puducherry and J&K assemblies follow their own statutes and enabling frameworks. Avoid copying Delhi's exact exclusions across UTs.
items.authority: Arts. 239, 239A, 239AA, Government of Union Territories Act 1963, J&K Reorganisation Act 2019
items.raw_authority: Arts. 239, 239A, 239AA, Government of Union Territories Act 1963, J&K Reorganisation Act 2019

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.distinction: Consists of persons registered in electoral rolls for the village within the panchayat area. Powers and functions depend on state law, with PESA applying in Scheduled Areas.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.distinction: Village-chair election follows state law. Intermediate and district chairs are elected **by and from among** elected members.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.prompt: Panchayat chair — vote and reserved offices
items.distinction: Chair and other members have voting rights in panchayat meetings under Art. 243C(4). At least one-third of chairperson offices at each level are reserved for women.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.distinction: State population **not exceeding** 20 lakh can omit the intermediate tier. “Below” would wrongly exclude a state with exactly 20 lakh.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.distinction: Five years runs from the date **appointed for the first meeting**, and a replacement after early dissolution serves the remainder. The six-month election exception is when the remainder is **less than six months**.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.prompt: Minimum age for panchayat and municipality
items.distinction: The constitutional disqualification rule protects a person aged at least 21 from disqualification on the ground of being under 25. Eligibility otherwise depends on the applicable law.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.distinction: At least one-third of directly elected seats are reserved for women including SC/ST women. Municipality chairperson reservation follows state law under Art. 243T(4).
items.authority: Arts. 243D, 243T · PYQ 2026 on SC/ST women in panchayats [P6]
items.raw_authority: Arts. 243D, 243T · **PYQ 2026** on SC/ST women in panchayats [P6]

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.distinction: Wards Committees apply from **3 lakh** municipal population. Metropolitan area definition uses **10 lakh or more**, besides the other constitutional conditions.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.distinction: At least four-fifths of the DPC are elected by and from elected members of district-level panchayat and municipalities in the district, as specified. For MPC the elected share is at least two-thirds from municipal elected members and panchayat chairpersons in the area.

items.subject: Polity
items.section_title: B8. Local Government Offices & Committees
items.prompt: Part IX and Part IXA exclusions
items.distinction: Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas and other constitutionally specified cases require checking the exact Part and Article. PESA extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule Scheduled Areas with modifications.

items.distinction: It may recommend relief or prosecution and approach courts. The armed-forces complaint route uses a Central Government report. The Act's one-year inquiry bar has a specific statutory formulation.

items.distinction: NCDRC is created by Consumer Protection Act 2019. Law Commission is constituted by executive notification and makes recommendations. NCBC is the constitutional member of the comparison.

items.distinction: CVC is statutory. CBI's existence stems from executive resolution and its police powers come from the DSPE Act. CVC's superintendence of DSPE concerning corruption matters has a defined statutory scope.

items.section_title: C1. Criminal Justice & Public Order (BNS, BNSS, BSA)

items.section_title: C1. Criminal Justice & Public Order (BNS, BNSS, BSA)
items.distinction: Section 479 generally uses **one-half** of the maximum sentence and **one-third** for a first-time offender, with an exclusion where death or life imprisonment is specified as a punishment, and separate conditions including multiple pending offences or cases.
